blurb:
Laredos is our go-to when someone in the family says they want Mexican and nobody wants to debate about it. Colorful inside, traditional decor, the whole cantina feel. Great for a casual weeknight dinner, a group outing, or honestly any time you want a margarita with your chips and salsa without making a production of it.

They do Mexican favorites the way you'd expect from a place like this. Classic dishes, solid margaritas, nothing too complicated. My wife and I have gone here plenty of times when we just needed an easy dinner out and didn't want to overthink it.

Prices are on the lower end, which makes it easy to say yes to the margarita. They're open every day of the week, and they run until 10:30 on Friday and Saturday nights if you're getting a late start.

blurb:
If you live near Roswell Road and you haven't been to JJ's yet, I get it. I put it off too. Don't. This is a neighborhood pizza spot that punches above its weight. Good for a game night, a casual Friday, grabbing a pie with the family, or just when you need comfort food without any fuss.

The stuffed pizza is the thing people won't shut up about, and for good reason. Get the garlic cheese knots too. One reviewer called them some of the best they've ever had, and that's not something people say lightly when it comes to garlic knots. My wife and I split those as a starter now every single time.

Just know they're closed on Tuesdays. If you show up on a Tuesday you're going to be standing in a parking lot feeling disappointed, and that's on you.

blurb:
If you're looking for a solid brunch spot in Marietta that won't let you down, Hamp and Harry's on Roswell Street is the answer. The service gets mentioned constantly in reviews, and for good reason. Attentive, friendly, and they actually take care of you. Good for a weekend brunch, a weekday lunch, or a Friday night out since they stay open until midnight on Fridays.

The fried chicken biscuit is what people keep coming back for. Hot, fluffy biscuit, big enough that you might be taking some of it home. The salad dressing gets called out specifically in reviews too, which tells you they're paying attention to the details most places skip.

Monday brunch hours start at 10am, and they open at 10am on weekends as well, so no sleeping in required to get there before they stop serving.

blurb:
This place is one of those spots you stumble into once and then suddenly find yourself going back every weekend. Brazilian Bakery Cafe on Powers Ferry is a cheerful little cafe that does Brazilian light bites alongside traditional cakes and cookies. Good for a slow Saturday morning, a quick weekday coffee run, or anytime you want something a little different than your usual bakery stop.

The traditional cakes and cookies are the real draw here. These are not your standard American bakery pastries. They have that distinct Brazilian style, and people who know that kind of food get very excited about it. Worth grabbing a few things to try even if you don't know exactly what you're looking at.

They're open until 10pm every night, which is pretty generous for a bakery. Sunday mornings they open a bit later at 8am, so plan accordingly if you're an early riser.

blurb:
Lemon Grass is where my wife and I end up when we want Thai and we want it to actually be good. It's on Roswell Road, spacious inside with a lot of red in the decor, and it has that comfortable sit-down feel that makes it work for a weeknight dinner or a nicer date night out. The 4.6 rating across nearly a thousand reviews tells you people are not complaining.

They do Thai noodles, curries, and the classics you'd expect. If you like your food with real heat, ask for it. They know what they're doing with spice levels. The curries in particular have a following with the regulars.

Fair warning on timing: they break between lunch and dinner every day, closing around 2:30pm and reopening at 5pm. They're also closed on Sundays and Saturday lunch service is dinner only. Plan ahead and you'll be fine.
